description: One-way ratchet on ESLint warnings, counted by scripts/run-lint.mjs from a single ESLint run. totals.warningCeiling replaces the hand-typed --max-warnings number that used to live in package.json: it is the exact measured count, may only fall, and is the value npm run lint enforces. perRule freezes each rule at its own count so a drawdown in one rule cannot silently pay for a regression in another - removing 500 `any` annotations while adding 500 react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warnings is a net loss that a single total would report as progress. step is the drawdown unit: when measured warnings sit a full step under the ceiling, scripts/audit-lint-warnings.mjs asks for the gain to be locked in. Lower a ceiling in the same change that removes the warnings - leaving headroom lets it refill silently.

notes.@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any: Exactly the type-escape backlog seen from ESLint: 11,440 = the 11,442 in config/type-escape-boundaries.json minus its 2 suppressions, which are not an ESLint rule. The binding gate for this rule stays config/type-escape-boundaries.json, which freezes every file individually and is therefore strictly stronger than a repository total. This ceiling exists so the two cannot disagree - it must be lowered whenever the type-escape ceiling is.
notes.errorCeiling: Zero and permanent. ESLint errors are not part of the drawdown; the ratchet governs warnings only.
